Computer Science and Information Science - EAS PhD program option
The Computer Science and Information Science option within the EAS PhD program offers advanced study and research opportunities in various disciplines related to modern information processing using computer programs and systems. Information science is highly interdisciplinary and is concerned with the analysis, collection, classification, manipulation, storage, retrieval and dissemination of information. Computer science deals with the theoretical foundations of computational methods for information creation and manipulation. Research opportunities span a wide range of theoretical and application topics including advanced software engineering, artificial intelligence, computer networks, computer vision and graphics, databases, data science, distributed algorithms and systems, formal methods, informatics, human-computer interaction, machine learning, mobile computing and cyber security, optical networks, programming languages, real-time systems, robotics, and wireless networks. Career opportunities are plentiful in the areas of information technology, business/financial, engineering and industry, health and human services, and government/public policy, both in industry and academia.
Course requirements
Core course credits - 15
Total core and research credits - 48
Elective course credits - 18
Total program credits - 66
Total program courses - 13
Core and Research Course Requirements
Five core courses (15 credits) are taken early in the program of study to ensure preparation in the fundamental research and analytical methods in the field.
EAS 501 - Advanced Mathematical Methods Credits: 3
EAS 502 - Numerical Methods Credits: 3
CIS 580 - Paradigmatic Sftware Dev Credits: 3
CIS 560 - Theoretical Comp Science Credits: 3
Or
ECE 565 - Operating Systems Credits: 3
CIS 570 - Adv Computer Systems Credits: 3
Or
ECE 562 - Advanced Computer Architecture Credits: 3
EAS 600 - Dissertation Proposal Preparation Credits: 3
EAS 602 - Research Ethics Credits: 1
EAS 700 - Doctoral Seminar Credits: 2
EAS 601 - Pre-Dissertation Research Credits: variable; .00 to 12.00
At most 15 credits of EAS 601 must be completed and
the total number of research credits (EAS 601 + EAS 701) must equal 27 credits.
EAS 701 - Doctoral Dissertation Research Credits: variable; 1.00 to 12.00
Elective Course Requirements and Choices
Elective courses (18 credits) help the student attain depth in focused areas within CSIS as well as breadth in a minor area of study. Major electives are drawn from computer science/engineering and from decision information sciences.
Major electives: choose 4 of CIS/ECE 500-600 level offerings
Minor electives: choose 2 of CEN/MNE/MTH/PHY 500-600 level offerings
Prerequisite, Concentration or Other Requirements
Ph.D. Qualifying Examination (QE) and Comprehensive Exam (CE): Each student must pass a qualifying exam and a comprehensive exam on research preparedness prior to becoming a doctoral candidate.
Qualifying Exam Waiver: If a candidate has an average GPA ≥ 3.5 in the CSIS core courses, the QE is waived.
